chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Adami, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Zayyat, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'I have performed zihar with my wife.' He asked me, 'How?' I said, 'I said to her,

key_terms.الظَّهَار: Zihar (a form of irrevocable divorce by comparison)
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: Like the back of my mother (the formula of Zihar)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zihar if a husband says 'You are to me like the back of my mother' without adding a condition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) distinguishes between a conditional vow of Zihar and an absolute declaration, ruling that mere utterance without a specific trigger incurs no expiation (kaffarah). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on intent and conditionality in marital vows, contrasting with some Sunni schools that may require expiation for the formula itself. The Imam’s instruction to 'not repeat' it serves as a preventive measure to avoid accidental binding of the vow.
